findings.evidence: Contrast. Weak: "Two weeks is really tight; we'll try our best." Strong: "Six weeks of work won't fit in two..."
findings.fix: Keep the "hidden risk" rationale in the bullet at line 62 and drop the weak/strong contrast, or fold it into references/expectation-alignment.md. The model already writes this kind of pushback, so the contrast is mostly activation content.

findings.evidence: Section 2 routes six scenarios through a table and sections 3-6 give process steps, so it mixes Navigation and Process patterns without a clear checkpoint order.
findings.fix: Add one line after the table saying to run section 3's pre-send gate on every path that produces a draft. Say that sections 4-6 are the entry points for receiving, resets and follow-up.

findings.evidence: The Gotchas list covers only the giving side and third parties. The Receive section (line 46) has no NEVER item.
findings.fix: Add a gotcha such as: "Never have the user concede or deny the label ('yes, I'm unreliable' or 'that's untrue') in the meeting. Conceding accepts the label, and denying turns it into a dispute with no instance to check."

findings.evidence: The description is dense, about 920 of 1024 characters. It is close to the limit and leaves little room for later trigger tuning.
findings.fix: Prepare, deliver, receive and follow up on specific workplace feedback using Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI), and reset stakeholder expectations with explicit scope/date trade-offs. Use when thanking a teammate for specific work, raising an observable behavior (broken builds, missed commitments, interrupting), answering vague criticism such as "you're unreliable" even if the user never says feedback, prepping a 1:1 or upward feedback, mediating two people you lead, writing the follow-up recap, or pushing back on a deadline or scope creep. Not for ceremonial congratulations, legal or HR determinations, PIPs, ratings, policy drafting, or layoffs and salary talks (use difficult-workplace-conversations).

findings.evidence: Assertions such as "Avoids character judgments and absolute language such as “always”" and "Includes an invitation for the teammate’s perspective and a specific next step" are only loosely verifiable. The first three evals have no input files. No script tests are needed because there is no scripts/ directory.
findings.fix: Make these assertions observable. For example: "The draft contains no sentence with always/never/you are" and "The draft ends with a question about the teammate's view and names one next action with an owner".

findings.evidence: Section 6 says to send a written recap with "each agreed action with owner and date, each disputed item marked open, and the check-in", but gives no template or example. Requests that mix recognition with corrective feedback are also not routed.
findings.fix: Add a 5-line recap template (Agreed: action / owner / date; Open: item; Check-in: date). Add a Section 2 rule for mixed requests: deliver recognition and corrective feedback separately and never put them in the same conversation or message.
